_notes: ONE LADDER FOR EVERY FACTION (Kyle, 2026-10-27: 'keep the wow tiers of rep... there will be a lot').
The tiers below are the WoW-standard eight and they are defined ONCE, here, shared by every faction.
A faction block carries only who it is, where its reputation comes from, and what standing buys - never
its own ladder. That is what lets one UI tab list fifty factions without fifty different scales, and it
means adding a faction is a block of data and nothing else.
Thresholds are cumulative from Neutral, exactly as WoW: Friendly 3000, Honored 9000, Revered 21000,
Exalted 42000. Negative standing is defined too - nothing in the game drives rep down yet, but the
ladder has to support it before something does, or the first hostile faction rewrites this file.
THE NUMBERS DO TWO DIFFERENT JOBS. A zone's quests are worth enough together to carry a player into
Revered - that is the real path and the one that tells the story. Exalted is finished on kills, and
only kills from enemies the faction has an actual stake in. There is deliberately no flat 'dungeon
mobs give rep' rule: it would make the optimal play farming the easiest trash in the easiest room,
and killing a mushroom should not earn standing with a library.

crimson_codex.name: The Crimson Codex
crimson_codex.description: Blood elf arcanists who went down a hole beneath the Ruins of Dalaran and never came back up.

leader.title: Codex-Master
leader.name: Ilarien Duskwaking
leader.line: Eleven thousand entries and the cavern keeps handing me things I have no column for. Do not take that as an invitation.

crimson_codex._lore_note: Shown on the faction's detail panel. Written as the Codex would have it written - they are the ones keeping the record, and they are not neutral about themselves.
lore: The fissure opened in ground the blood elves had already surveyed. One of them put a boot through what should have been solid rock above the Ruins of Dalaran, and the hole went down past the reach of every lamp they were carrying.

Below it they found a cavern wide enough to hold weather, lit by something hanging at the centre of it that none of them has reached. They have been down there ever since. They call it a find rather than a discovery, because a find is something that was already there, waiting.

Their work is the index. Every crystal, every column, every stand of fungus gets a number and a place in the ledger. Lately the ledger has begun to fail them. There is Dalaran stone far beneath Dalaran that no cart ever carried down. There is crystal growing in figures too exact for honest stone. And under the Sporefall something has been reading their notes through the mould in their own camp, and writing back.

They are precise, dry, and a good deal more frightened than they let on. They also came through the same change you did. Nobody in Kael's Bastion has an older claim on any of it, and every one of them knows it.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. kill_boss objectives pay the boss rate; the named capstones pay more.

_comment: Only enemies the Codex has a stake in. Dissidents are ex-colleagues, Interlopers are rivals for
the same dig, Revenants sit on the prize, and the Deep Bloom is the thing reading them back.
The wildlife pays nothing, however deep the cave it lives in.
Gates, not a displayed ladder (the faction panel stays information only).

orgrimmar.name: Orgrimmar
orgrimmar.description: The orc capital: raised fast out of red stone and ship timber by people who could not afford to be particular.

leader.title: Warchief
leader.name: Thrall
leader.line: We were given nothing. We took a desert and made a home of it. I will not stand here and apologise for the taking.

lore: The Horde came ashore in Durotar with what it could carry, and Orgrimmar went up out of red stone and the timbers of the ships that brought it. The city still looks like what it is: built fast, by people who couldn't afford to be choosy.

Thrall holds it. He was born in chains and got his people out of them, and it left him careful. He'd rather keep what the Horde has than reach for more, and there are voices in the city who say so, loudly and often.
The city keeps its regard in quartermasters' ledgers: who held the Barrens road, who went down into the Chasm when the Burning Blade came up out of it, who was on the wall when it mattered.

When the world changed, Orgrimmar opened its gates to the people it threw up faster than anywhere else on the continent, and with less argument. Thrall's never said why in public. The ones who were in the internment camps with him have never needed him to.

kill_rep._comment: The Horde's standing enemies in its own territory - the cult under the city, the centaur on the Barrens road, the quilboar in the fields, the harpies on the ridge.

darkspear_tribe.name: The Darkspear Tribe
darkspear_tribe.description: Jungle trolls who were down to their last island, and have never once let anyone call what happened next a rescue.

leader.title: Elder
leader.name: Kang'ari
leader.line: We been run off dis water before, mon. We came back. Dat is most of what you need to know about us.

lore: The Darkspear were down to their last island when the Horde found them. It was a bargain between two peoples with nothing, and the trolls have kept their half of it to the letter ever since.
Then Zalazane took the isles. He went through the tribe with hex and voodoo until their own kin came out of the surf at them, and the Darkspear pulled back to the mainland and started again.
They don't say the isles are lost. They say the ones still out on the water aren't back yet, and they'll correct you if you say it the other way.
The tribe keeps its own spiritwalkers, its own trainers and its own account of who stood with it when things were bad. That account is older than the Horde's, and it isn't the same list.

kill_rep._comment: Zalazane's hexed and the naga on the reefs - the two things keeping the tribe off its own islands.

the_forsaken.name: The Forsaken
the_forsaken.description: The dead of Lordaeron, who woke with their minds intact and took the ruin of their capital back.

leader.title: Banshee Queen
leader.name: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner
leader.line: We were not given our freedom. I took it, and I will not be asked to be grateful for a thing I had to tear loose.

lore: The Scourge raised Lordaeron's dead and set them walking. Then its hold on them slipped, and what straightened up in the ruins remembered everything: names, houses, the faces of their families, and exactly what had been done to them.

They took the undercroft beneath the palace and made a country of it. The throne room overhead still has the old king's blood dried into the floor, and nobody down there calls that a tragedy. It's theirs now.

The Apothecarium sits at the heart of the city and worries everyone, allies included. It's the only place on the continent studying the plague that made them. Ask the apothecaries why and they'll tell you it's for a cure. Read their ledgers and you may come to another answer.

What they won't forgive is the Scarlet Crusade, who kill them on sight for the crime of having been murdered, and the cults still working for the thing that did it. Standing with the Forsaken is mostly a tally of how many of either you've put back in the ground.
They're tired, blackly funny and very hard to impress. They've been dead a while, and there isn't much left that surprises them.

kill_rep._comment: The Scarlet Crusade, who kill them on sight, and the cults still serving the thing that made them.

steamwheedle_cartel.name: The Steamwheedle Cartel
steamwheedle_cartel.description: Goblin traders who will sell to anyone, protect no one, and keep a port open through wars that shut everything else.

leader.title: Boss
leader.name: Gazlowe
leader.line: Neutral ain't a principle, friend. It's a business model, and it's the only one that keeps a port open when everyone on both sides wants it.

lore: The Cartel isn't a nation and has never pretended to be. It's a company with harbours, and those harbours are the only stretches of coast where a Horde ship and an Alliance ship tie up at the same pier and nothing happens.

The neutrality is what it sells. Bring a war into Ratchet and the goblins won't take a side. They'll put you on a boat, bill your faction for the trouble, and have the dock working again by the evening tide.
Gazlowe runs the port, and runs it better than its margins deserve. He's turned down three offers to move the whole operation somewhere richer, and nobody in Ratchet knows why.

Their regard is bought rather than earned, and they're honest about it. Pirates on the water and bandits on the Barrens road cost the Cartel money. Anyone who brings that number down is good for business, and in Ratchet that's as close to friendship as it gets.

kill_rep._comment: Whatever interrupts trade: pirates on the water, bandits on the Barrens road. The Cartel pays per head and does not care about your politics.

thunder_bluff.name: Thunder Bluff
thunder_bluff.description: The tauren of a city that fell when the world changed, still carrying its name.
thunder_bluff.home_name: Camp Taurajo, the Southern Barrens - in exile

leader.title: Elder
leader.name: Longtread
leader.line: The seat is his. I stand near it. I will go on standing near it until somebody puts a reason in my hand.

thunder_bluff._leader_note: Longtread speaks for the tauren and holds no title. Cairne was LOST when the city fell - never found, never buried - so the office is not vacant so much as unresolved, and taking it would be a ruling nobody is willing to make.
lore: Thunder Bluff stood on four rock spires above Mulgore, and no army ever took it. When the world changed, the ground under the spires gave way, and the city went down with it.

Mulgore's still there, after a fashion. The grass grows and the sky's where it should be, but the plain itself is wrong now, and the things that walk it kill war parties without slowing down. The tauren have gone back for the spires four times. Three of those war parties came home.

Cairne Bloodhoof was in the city when it fell, and nothing of him has been found. There's no body to burn and nothing to bury, so the chieftain's seat stands empty. Elder Longtread speaks for the tauren, and he's turned the title down every time it's been offered, because taking it would mean Cairne is dead, and nobody's proved that.

They live as guests now: at Camp Taurajo, with the warbands in the southern Barrens, and in other people's towns, more of them every season. Every nation that took them in asked nothing for it. The tauren pay it back in work, on every wall and every road they're given.
They still call themselves Thunder Bluff. It's the name of a people now, not of a place, and it'll stay that way until they stand on the spires again.

kill_rep._comment: What presses on the ground they have left: quilboar raiding the camps, and the Bael'dun dwarves digging a plain that is not theirs while the tauren watch a worse one from a distance.

booty_bay_authority.name: The Booty Bay Port Authority
booty_bay_authority.description: A goblin harbour that stopped being a franchise and started behaving like a government.

leader.title: Baron
leader.name: Baron Revilgaz
leader.line: The Cartel will tell you this is their port. Let them. They are four thousand miles away and I am standing on it.

booty_bay_authority._lore_note: Shown on the faction's detail panel. Written from the harbour's side of the argument, because the harbour is the one winning it.
lore: There's no road into Stranglethorn. The range closed the land route and never opened it again, which left two ways in: an airship berth the Horde flew in over the top, and this cove.

That made Booty Bay the only deep-water harbour still joining anything to anything, and a harbour in that position stops taking instructions. The Baron didn't declare anything. He just started deciding which hulls left on which tide, and after the third season nobody was asking Ratchet.
The Steamwheedle Cartel hasn't formally lost the port, and it'll tell you so at length. Factor Weezel still signs the manifests and still files them, and the Baron still decides what sails.

What the Authority sells is what the Cartel always sold, a pier where two enemies can tie up and nothing happens, except that here it's enforced rather than negotiated. The bruisers are the law, the Baron is the court, and the tariff isn't up for discussion. People complain about the landing fee until the first time they need the harbour to hold.

quest_rep._comment: Honored is the ceiling on quests alone. Everything below is authored in Booty Bay and the southern jungle - the Authority does not pay for work done north of the Gurbashi, because north of the Gurbashi is Orgrimmar's problem.

kill_rep._comment: What costs the harbour money. Bloodsail on the water above all - a pirate in the shallows is a hull that does not arrive - plus the naga sitting on the drowned terraces the Authority would very much like to salvage. Jungle wildlife pays nothing: it has never cost anyone a cargo.

the_ashclaim.name: The Ashclaim
the_ashclaim.description: Dark Iron dwarves and goblins reclaiming a city that is legally one dwarf's and practically nobody's.

leader.title: Thane of Khaz Varun
leader.name: Durgan Ashhold
leader.line: My great-grandfather's hall is four hundred feet down and full of things that used to be my cousins. The goblins have given me a figure for clearing it. I have signed it. Do not ask me what it was.

the_ashclaim._lore_note: Written as the Ashclaim would have it written - a prospectus, not a history. The thane supplies the claim and the goblins supply everything else, and both of them describe that arrangement as generous of themselves.
lore: Khaz Varun went dark long before the Integration, and the Ashholds have carried the deed from hall to rented room to a bunk on a goblin barge for as long as anyone has bothered to count.
What changed is that the sea route opened. A deed nobody could reach is a story; a deed four days from Saltspur is an asset, and the goblins can read an asset at a distance.

So the thane holds the claim and the underwriters hold the paper on the claim, and a wharf went up on the north-east shore inside a season. The hold behind it is built from the old city's own salvaged stone, which the dwarves consider a homecoming and the goblins consider freight they did not have to buy.

Neither half of the Ashclaim agrees on what the isle is for. The thane wants his ancestors' hall emptied of whatever is living in it now. The underwriters want the foundry lit and earning, and have observed in writing that those two things are not the same dig.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. Matches the Crimson Codex rates so nothing new needs tuning.

_comment: Only enemies the Ashclaim has a stake in: the mad dwarves squatting in Khaz Varun hold the prize,
rival salvagers are after the same wrecks, and these elementals are actively breaking the works.
Island wildlife and the deep-volcano elementals pay nothing - farming a corridor must never beat
running a dungeon.

emerald_reclamation.name: The Emerald Reclamation
emerald_reclamation.description: Night elves, Timbermaw furbolgs, the forest's own treants and a fair number of transplants, taking Felwood back from the Legion one grove at a time.

leader.title: Arch Druid
leader.name: Aelyra Moonbough
leader.line: Nobody here agrees on much. The Sentinels want the Legion dead, the Timbermaw want their cousins back, the trees want to be left alone, and the transplants want somewhere that stays put. It turns out all four of those are the same job.

emerald_reclamation._lore_note: Kyle, 14 Nov 2026: 'its a group thing, whole new faction!' Four peoples who'd never have shared a fire before the Integration, and one forest they all need.
lore: Felwood was lost long before the Integration. The Sentinels held a few watchtowers in the south, the Timbermaw held their tunnels in the north, and everything between belonged to the Legion's leftovers and the furbolgs it drove mad.

What changed was people. Three years ago the forest filled up with transplants who'd lost everything else, and a lot of them would rather plant something than wait for a rescue that wasn't coming. The druids needed hands. The Timbermaw needed somebody who didn't flinch at them.

The first glade the druids cleansed became Emerald Sanctuary. The second became a reason to try a third. The South is green again now, all the way up to the Fel Line, and the Reclamation means to keep walking north.
The treants never joined anything. They just started standing where the Sentinels stood, and nobody has been foolish enough to ask them to move.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. Matches the Crimson Codex and Ashclaim rates.

_comment: Only what the Reclamation is fighting: the Legion and what the fel has taken. The South's
wildlife and treants pay nothing - they're the forest the Reclamation is trying to give back.

the_unnamed.description: Somebody keeps a ledger of the places that were never on any map, and of everyone who's walked out of one alive. You've never met them. Your name is in it anyway, and the line under it gets a little longer every time.
_comment: SECRET (tools/build_unnamed_faction.py, Kyle 15 Nov 2026). The journal shows only 'Current Status: <tier>';
combat never prints its gains; nothing in the game says where it comes from (any boss in a frontier zone,
50 a kill). Its seller is parked: vendor_stock_unplaced is read by nothing until he is placed.

pale_flame.name: The Order of the Pale Flame
pale_flame.description: A holy order led by Earth transplants who walked out of the Scarlet Crusade. They hunt the mindless dead and the Crusade's fanatics, and they leave the thinking dead alone.
pale_flame.home_name: The Bulwark, on the road from Tirisfal into the Plaguelands

leader.title: Flamekeeper
leader.name: Rory Callahan
leader.location: The Bulwark, at the keep in the Order's quarter
leader.line: I wore the red for a year. When I took it off, I kept the flame and scraped the colour out of it, and that's the whole of what we are.

pale_flame._lore_note: Kyle, 16 Nov 2026: 'the leader and top fighters are FROM EARTH' and 'The leader WAS part of the Scarlet Crusade though! that is Important!'. A mix of the Argent Dawn and the Crusade.
lore: In the first year of the Integration, the Scarlet Crusade was the only army in Lordaeron killing what was killing everyone. A lot of transplants joined it, because it was there and it was winning.

Rory Callahan was one of them. He was an ironworker from Boston by way of Cork, and he was good at it. He lasted a year. He left the night the Crusade burned a camp of transplants for keeping company with the Forsaken, and the best of the people around him left with him.

They kept the flame and scraped the red out of it. The Order of the Pale Flame hunts the mindless dead, the Cult of the Damned, and the Crusade's fanatics. It doesn't hunt the Forsaken, and some of its members hate that rule more than any other.
The Argent Dawn calls them Scarlets with better manners. The Order calls the Argent Dawn slow. They share what they learn about Scholomance and Stratholme anyway, because neither can afford not to.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. Matches the other factions' rates.
quest_rep._comment_zones: A zone's quests pay one faction (qa_factions). The Order's are the West; the Argent Dawn's are the East. The Order's chains that run into the East go in `also`.

_comment: Scarlet fanatics only. Open-world Scarlets pay a little and stop at Honored (Kyle: 'Little until
honored'). The Scarlet Monastery pays more and also stops at Honored; Hearthglen and Stratholme's
Scarlet half don't stop. [amount, cap tier] is a capped kill (world/faction_manager.py).

argent_dawn.name: The Argent Dawn
argent_dawn.description: The order at Light's Hope that fights the Scourge without asking who its soldiers used to be. Natives, transplants and a few Forsaken stand its walls.

leader.title: Commander
leader.name: Eligor Dawnbringer
leader.line: We don't ask where you came from. We ask whether you'll stand on the wall tonight, and most people say yes.

lore: The Argent Dawn was holding the line against the Scourge before the Integration, and it's still holding it. It takes anyone who'll stand on the wall, which these days means a lot of transplants.
Light's Hope Chapel is the order's heart: a chapel on holy ground the dead can't cross, and the last place in the east where you can sleep without someone on watch.
It trades in Scourgestones, the shards of necromancy the dead carry, and it pays well for them. It doesn't much like the Order of the Pale Flame, and it works with them every week.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. Matches the other factions' rates.

_comment: The Scourge (Kyle, 16 Nov 2026: 'Argent Dawn from killing Scourge'): every undead and every Cult of the Damned member in the Plaguelands pays a little, rares more, up to Honored. Past Honored it's Scourgestones at Light's Hope, quests, and Scholomance and Stratholme's undead half.

timbermaw_hold.name: Timbermaw Hold
timbermaw_hold.description: The Timbermaw furbolgs of the hold above Felwood: the last of their people the fel didn't take, and they mean to take their cousins back.
timbermaw_hold.home_name: Timbermaw Hold, in Azshara (its people also keep the Timbermaw Tunnel above Felwood)

leader.title: Elder
leader.name: Haldor Mossmane
leader.location: The Elders' Great Lodge, in Timbermaw Hold
leader.line: Every Deadwood in Felpaw was born in the Hold, or their mother was. We don't hate them. We can't afford to stop fighting them, either.

timbermaw_hold._lore_note: Kyle, 17 Nov 2026: 'add timbermaw hold ... and we can add the reputation'.
lore: The Timbermaw's home is the Hold in Azshara, and their tunnels run through the mountains from there to Felwood, Winterspring and Moonglade. They were the only furbolgs the fel never took, because they kept to the mountain and kept their own counsel.
Their cousins weren't so lucky. The Deadwood tribes of Felwood drank the corruption with the water, and they've been raiding the forest ever since. Felpaw Village is the worst of them.

The day the world changed, the roof came down on the tunnel's Winterspring and Moonglade passages. The Elders took it as a sign to look south instead, and for the first time in a long time they opened the tunnel's Felwood mouth to outsiders who'd help. The Moonglade passage has since been dug out from the glade's side; Winterspring's is still shut.
They trade with the Emerald Reclamation and they like its druids, but the Hold keeps its own counsel and its own ledger. The Timbermaw remember every favour, and every insult, for a very long time.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. Matches the other factions' rates.
quest_rep._comment_rate: 325 a quest, not the 225 most factions pay: the Timbermaw own eight quests and the feathers, and questing has to show on the bar (qa_factions).

_comment: The Deadwood (Classic's Timbermaw rep): 10 a kill and Grimpelt 50, up to Honored. Past Honored it's Deadwood Headdress Feathers at the Hold and the Hold's quests.

sunreach_conclave.name: The Sunreach Conclave
sunreach_conclave.description: Blood elf magisters who lit Firstlight Spire on Dawnhaven, and who mean to take back what their ancestors lost on the Azshara coast now that the sea is giving Zin-Azshari back.
sunreach_conclave.home_name: Firstlight Spire, on Dawnhaven off the Azshara coast (with a field camp at Talrendis Landing)

leader.title: Grand Magister
leader.name: Velanthe Sunreach
leader.location: The Conclave Hall, beside the spire, Firstlight Spire
leader.line: I watched the last spires of Quel'Thalas fall into a sea that wasn't there the day before. I won't watch our history go the same way. I want it back, all of it, the good and the shameful.

sunreach_conclave._lore_note: Kyle, 17-18 Nov 2026: the Sunreach Conclave, its own TBC shelf, its leader quest-free and movable; 'Proud, fair magister'.
lore: When the worlds merged, the sea came up over the last of Quel'Thalas's coast. The magisters who got out took ship south and found Azshara's shore rising instead: Zin-Azshari, the city their ancestors left ten thousand years ago, coming back up out of the water.

Grand Magister Velanthe Sunreach gathered them into the Conclave. They mean to be standing on the shore when the city comes back, to take back what was theirs before anyone else can, and to learn what their ancestors did to make the gods sink it.

Their home is Dawnhaven, an island off the coast that the old high elves hid behind wardstones long before the change. The Conclave found it empty, its outpost dead and its Lightwell dark, and took it back. They lit the spire at its head again after a thousand years and called it Firstlight, and anyone the sea washes up on its shore gets a room there, elf or not.

The Grand Magister and her quartermaster keep the Conclave Hall beside the spire now. The work on the coast goes on from Talrendis Landing, which they share with Orgrimmar's salvage crews, because the Warchief has the muscle and they have the magic. Neither side likes the arrangement, and both sides keep two lists of everything that comes out of the ground.

the_liquidators.name: The Liquidators
the_liquidators.description: Earth transplants who've lived beside a fallout zone, or cleaned one up, holding the line in Deadwind Pass with the Forsaken apothecaries.

leader.title: Chief Liquidator
leader.name: Halyna Bondar
leader.line: My father was a liquidator at Chernobyl in 1986. He came home, and he didn't talk about it, and he kept his dosimeter on the kitchen shelf for the rest of his life. I know why now.

the_liquidators._lore_note: Kyle, 18 Nov 2026: 'the liquidators get their own faction'.
lore: When the worlds came together, the leylines under Deadwind Pass tore open, and the fallout came out of the tear. The Forsaken call it the Seep. The transplants who'd seen something like it before call it what it is.

They came from Slavutych and Fukushima, from the farms under Windscale, from Semey beside the Polygon, from Rongelap and Goiania and Hanford and St. George, Utah. They came on purpose, and they took the word their parents' generation used for the people who went into Chernobyl: liquidators.

They hold Ariden's Watch with the Forsaken apothecaries, who can walk where the living can't. Everyone scrubs at the troughs, everyone carries a dosimeter, and every name goes on the board by the pyre.
The Undercity supplies them. Nobody commands them, which is why the Forsaken let them stay.

cenarion_circle.name: The Cenarion Circle
cenarion_circle.description: The druids of Moonglade, night elf and tauren together, keeping the glade and watching over every land that's fallen sick.

leader.title: Keeper of Nighthaven
leader.name: Rabine Saturna
leader.line: The Circle was here before the worlds came together, and it'll be here after whatever's waking has finished waking. That's not a boast. It's a promise we made a long time ago.

cenarion_circle._lore_note: Kyle, 18 Nov 2026: 'the cenarion circle is still there' and 'true to lore'.
lore: The Cenarion Circle is the druids' order, night elf and tauren together, and Moonglade is its home. Keeper Remulos stands at his shrine on the lake's north-west shore, and the druids who walk the Emerald Dream sleep in the Barrow Dens.

When Thunder Bluff fell, the tauren druids who survived came up the mountain to the glade, and the Circle took them in. Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem leads them. The tauren half of Nighthaven is crowded and grieving and still makes room for anyone who comes.
The Circle watches the sick lands: Felwood, Azshara's rot, the Plaguelands and the wound in Deadwind. Lately it's been watching its own glade too, because something in Moonglade is waking up.
It's in good standing with the Wakened, the transplants who woke on its shore, and it argues with them about the Dream the way old friends argue.

the_wakened.name: The Wakened
the_wakened.description: Transplants who arrived asleep in Moonglade's grass, were woken by the druids, and stayed to understand the Dream from the outside.
the_wakened.home_name: The Wakened's settlement, on Moonglade's west shore

leader.title: Dr.
leader.name: Ingrid Sandvik
leader.line: Everyone here woke up in the same place, in the same grass, with a druid standing over them. What we do about that is up to us, and we've decided to do it together.

the_wakened._lore_note: Kyle, 18 Nov 2026: 'the Wakened ... transplant led ... in good standing' with the Circle.
lore: When the worlds came together, the Emerald Dream bled into Moonglade for a moment, and every transplant who came through anywhere near the glade arrived asleep. The druids found them lying in the grass round the lake and woke them one at a time.

Most of them stayed. They built a settlement on the west shore with their own hands, badly at first, and they carved the last thing each of them remembered from Earth into a wall that's now longer than their longhouse.
Not everyone woke. The ones who didn't sleep on in the Barrow Dens beside the druids, and the Wakened visit them.
Dr. Ingrid Sandvik leads them. She spent twenty years in Trondheim studying what people's brains do at night, and now she's studying the Dream from the only angle the druids never had: the outside.

feathermoon_sentinels.name: The Feathermoon Sentinels
feathermoon_sentinels.description: The night elf Sentinels of Feathermoon Stronghold, holding Feralas's coast from their island since long before the merge.
feathermoon_sentinels.home_name: Feathermoon Stronghold, on its island off the Forgotten Coast

leader.title: General
leader.name: Shandris Feathermoon
leader.location: Before the great hall, Feathermoon Stronghold
leader.line: I've held this island through wars that would have ended your world twice over. If you're here to help, there's work, and the Sentinels remember who helped.

feathermoon_sentinels._lore_note: Kyle, 19 Nov 2026: Feralas gets the Feathermoon Sentinels as its new faction; Mojache pays Orgrimmar. docs/feralas_brief.md.
lore: The Sentinels have kept Feathermoon Stronghold on its island off the Forgotten Coast for longer than most nations on Earth have existed. Shandris Feathermoon, General of the Sentinel Army, commands it herself.

When the worlds merged, a forest from somewhere else grew up on the coast in a single night, and a few of the people who came with it built a hollow under its trees. The Sentinels watched them from the walls for two years before they decided what to make of them.

Now the Hatecrest naga come up the beaches at night to dig in the old Highborne ruins, the Gordunni dig at Isildien, and the Sentinels have more coast to hold than they have sisters to hold it. Transplants are factionless, so Shandris lets them land and work, and remembers who does it well.

highbough_tribes.name: The Highbough Tribes
highbough_tribes.description: The trolls who climbed the World Tree and made it their home, from the landing at its roots to the Great Settlement in its heart.
highbough_tribes.home_name: The Great Settlement, in the heart of the World Tree

leader.title: High Chieftain
leader.name: Zan'kaji
leader.location: The Heart Palace, on the Chieftain's Rise in the Great Settlement
leader.line: The tree answered us when the world broke. We climbed it, and we'll keep it. Help us and you're one of the tribes.

highbough_tribes._lore_note: Kyle, 19 Nov 2026: the World Tree's town and faction are the trolls'. docs/worldtree_brief.md.
lore: Three years ago a seed split the reef off Stranglethorn's west coast, and the tree that came out of it has never stopped growing. Its roots drink the sea, its branches carry whole villages, and its crown has gone up through the clouds into Caelora, the Aetherians' sky.

Stranglethorn's trolls, squeezed between Grom'gol, the Bloodsail and their own feuding tribes, were the first to climb it. Darkspear kin and the tribes who'd broken with the Gurubashi feuds, with a few Skullsplitter and Bloodscalp who turned their backs on their own, built a landing at its roots and a city in its heart.
They call the tree a loa that answered them when nothing else would. The Highbough Tribes hold it now, allied to the Horde without answering to it, and they remember who helps them keep it.

aetherians.name: The Aetherians
aetherians.description: The scholar houses of Aurelion, who rule Caelora, the Aetherians' continent above the clouds, and the survey the House of the Patient Lens sent down to the World Tree.
aetherians.home_name: Aurelion, the city of the Aetherians, above the cloud

leader.title: First Speaker of the Council
leader.name: Aldren Sorvaine
leader.location: The Council Hall of the High Houses, on Aurelion's Council Ring
leader.line: The houses have argued for a hundred years about what the ground is worth. We're about to find out, because we can't hold up the sky without it.

aetherians._lore_note: Kyle, 19-20 Nov 2026: the Aetherian split (rep with the scholar houses, the Ascendancy is the enemy), Aurelion ruled by a council of houses, the houses divided on what's killing their world. docs/worldtree_brief.md.
lore: Above the clouds there's a continent nobody on the ground knew about. The Aetherians call it Caelora, and they've lived on its floating islands for as long as their records go back. They're tall and pale, with crystal growing along their arms and light in their eyes, and Aurelion, their capital, floats on engines of crystal older than any kingdom below.

Their sky has been dying for centuries, slowly, the way a fire goes out. The engines fail one by one, islands fall and the cloud thins, and lately it's all been going faster. The council of the scholar houses can't agree on why. Some houses say the World Tree should be studied before anyone touches it. The Ascendancy, their army, says the tree is the only thing in the sky still rising, and should simply be taken.

The House of the Patient Lens sent a survey down to the tree to meet the people living on it. It's the first time in their history the Aetherians have come down to the ground, and most of them still think the ground is primitive. The ones who've met it are starting to change their minds.
